questions.question: Where was the 7th Joint Group of Customs (JGC) Meeting between India and Bhutan held in April 2026?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Munnar, Kerala**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The **7th Joint Group of Customs (JGC) Meeting** between **India** and **Bhutan** was successfully conducted to discuss customs cooperation, trade facilitation, and border management.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meeting Location and Date:** The meeting was held in **Munnar, Kerala** on **20th–21st April 2026**.
 
• **Leadership:** It was co-chaired by Mr. **Yogendra Garg** (Special Secretary and Member (Customs), CBIC, India) and Mr. **Sonam Jamtsho** (Director General, Department of Revenue and Customs, Bhutan).
 
• **Purpose:** The JGC serves as an institutional framework for resolving bilateral issues relating to **customs cooperation**, **trade facilitation**, and **border management**.
 
• Therefore, the correct location for the 7th JGC Meeting is **Munnar, Kerala**, making Option 3 correct. While the Bhutanese delegation visited **Kochi Port**, the meeting itself was hosted in **Munnar**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bilateral Trade Overview:** **India** is Bhutan’s largest trading partner, accounting for nearly **80% of Bhutan’s total trade**. Trade exceeded **$1.9 billion in FY 2024–25**, showing a growth of over **46%**.
 
• **Border Infrastructure:** There are **10 notified land customs stations** along the India–Bhutan border. These are located in **West Bengal (6)** and **Assam (4)**.
 
• **Port Visit:** The delegation visited **Kochi Port** to observe maritime operations, including vessel berthing, container handling, and the **Automatic Identification System (AIS)** used in sea patrolling.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• Key priority areas discussed included **Coordinated Border Management (CBM)**, pre-arrival exchange of customs data, and facilitating transit cargo movement via the **Electronic Cargo Tracking System (ECTS)**.
 
• The meeting aimed to ensure secure border management under the **Agreement on Trade, Commerce and Transit** framework.

questions.question: India and the United Kingdom launched the Offshore Wind Taskforce under which vision framework?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vision 2035.**__

__
 
• **India and the United Kingdom launched the India-UK Offshore Wind Taskforce on February 18, 2026 under Vision 2035.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Taskforce was constituted under Vision 2035 and the Fourth India-UK Energy Dialogue.**
 
• **It aims to provide strategic leadership and coordination for India’s nascent offshore wind ecosystem.**
 
• **The initiative focuses on accelerating clean energy cooperation through time-bound and execution-focused collaboration.**
 
• **The framework strengthens India-UK bilateral cooperation in renewable energy, particularly offshore wind development.**

• **Offshore Wind Energy** refers to wind power projects installed in coastal waters, enabling higher efficiency due to stronger and more consistent wind speeds compared to onshore projects.
 
• **National Green Hydrogen Mission** is India’s flagship initiative to promote production and export of green hydrogen, supporting decarbonisation and energy security goals.

questions.question: Which countries are part of the IMEC alliance?

options.text: India, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Israel, European Union, USA
India, China, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Russia
India, Pakistan, UAE, Iran, European Union
India, UAE, Qatar, Turkey, European Union

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Israel, European Union, USA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC)** is a planned economic corridor that aims to bolster economic development by fostering connectivity and economic integration between **Asia**, the **Arabian Gulf**, and **Europe**.
 
• The project was launched on **September 9, 2023**, on the sidelines of the **G20 Summit** held in **New Delhi**, **India**.
 
• The signatories of the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) include **India**, the **United States of America**, the **United Arab Emirates (UAE)**, **Saudi Arabia**, the **European Union**, **France**, **Italy**, and **Germany**.
 
• While **Israel** was not an initial signatory to the MoU, it is a critical geographical and logistical partner in the alliance as the corridor is designed to pass through the **Port of Haifa** in **Israel** to connect to **Europe**. ***Hence, the option containing India, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Israel, European Union, and USA is correct.***
 
• The corridor is divided into two distinct parts: the **East Corridor**, which connects **India** to the **Arabian Gulf**, and the **Northern Corridor**, which connects the **Arabian Gulf** to **Europe**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Components of Infrastructure:** The **IMEC** alliance focuses on multiple layers of infrastructure including a **railway network** designed to provide a reliable and cost-effective **ship-to-rail transit**; an **electricity cable** network for renewable energy; and a **high-speed data cable** for digital connectivity.
 
• **Strategic Energy Goals:** A significant application of this corridor is the transport of **green hydrogen** via pipelines from **India** and the **Middle East** to **Europe**, aligning with global climate goals and **energy security**.
 
• **Economic Impact:** Experts suggest that the corridor will increase **trade efficiency** by reducing the transit time between **India** and **Europe** by **40%** and lowering transit costs by **30%** compared to existing maritime routes like the **Suez Canal**.
 
• **Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment (PGII):** The **IMEC** is considered a landmark project under the **PGII**, which is a **G7** initiative to fund infrastructure projects in developing nations, often viewed as a strategic alternative to **China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)**.
 
• **Geopolitical Context:** The project facilitates the normalization of ties in the **Middle East**, particularly between **Israel** and **Arab nations** like **Saudi Arabia** and the **UAE**, under the broader umbrella of **United States** diplomatic efforts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of the European Union:** As a single entity, the **European Union** coordinates the participation of its member states like **France**, **Germany**, and **Italy** to ensure seamless connectivity from the **Mediterranean ports** to mainland **Europe**.
 
• **Port of Haifa:** Located in **Israel**, this port is a vital link where the rail network from the **Arabian Peninsula** meets the sea route to **Piraeus** in **Greece** or other **European** ports.
 
• **India's Role:** For **India**, the corridor enhances **strategic autonomy** and provides a direct route to **European markets**, bypassing **Pakistan** and reducing dependency on the **International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC)** that passes through **Iran** and **Russia**.
 
• **Year of Implementation:** Following the **2023** announcement, member countries have committed to meeting regularly to develop a **technical design** and a **working timeline** for the phased construction of the rail and pipe links.

questions.question: The India–UK Critical Minerals Global Supply Chain Observatory (GSCO), launched in June 2026, is a joint initiative of which two academic and research institutions?

options.text: Indian Institute of Science (IISc) Bangalore and University of Oxford
Indian Institute of Technology (ISM) Dhanbad and University of Cambridge
Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi and Imperial College London
Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay and London School of Economics

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Institute of Technology (ISM) Dhanbad and University of Cambridge**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**
__
• The **India–UK Critical Minerals Global Supply Chain Observatory (GSCO)** was formally launched in **New Delhi** by the Union Minister of Coal and Mines, **Shri G. Kishan Reddy**, and UK Foreign Secretary **Yvette Cooper** on June 4, 2026.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**
__
• **Joint Initiative:** The Observatory is a collaboration between **TEXMiN** (Technology Innovation in Exploration & Mining Foundation) at the **Indian Institute of Technology (ISM) Dhanbad** and the **University of Cambridge**.
• **Purpose:** It is designed as a **data-driven platform** to monitor and analyze global critical mineral supply chains, identify **risks and disruptions**, and provide market intelligence for policymakers and industry.
• **National Alignment:** The initiative supports the objectives of India's **National Critical Mineral Mission (NCMM)** and the **India–UK Technology Security Initiative**.
• **Strategic Sectors:** It focuses on securing resources essential for **clean energy transitions**, **electric mobility**, **advanced manufacturing**, and emerging technologies.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
__
• The initiative was first announced during the **India–UK Prime Ministers' bilateral engagement** in **October 2025**.
• A formal **Research Collaboration Agreement** for the observatory was signed in **March 2026**.
• **TEXMiN** is supported by the **Department of Science and Technology (DST)**, Government of India.
** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

• The launch marks a milestone in **supply chain resilience** between India and the UK.
• The platform enables **evidence-based policymaking** by providing intelligence on critical minerals, which are considered the backbone of modern economies.

questions.question: What position did the European Union hold as a market for Indian seafood exports during 2025–26?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Third-largest**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Commerce & Industry** announced that the **European Union (EU)** has included **India** in its revised draft list for the continued export of **aquaculture products** to the European market from **September 2026**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• During **2025–26**, the **European Union** emerged as the **third-largest market** for **Indian seafood exports**.
 
• The EU accounted for **18.94 per cent** of the total export value, amounting to **US$ 1.593 billion**.
 
• Exports to the EU recorded significant growth over **2024–25**, with the export value rising by **41.45 per cent** and quantity by **38.29 per cent**.
 
• **Farmed shrimp** continued to constitute the major share of exports to the region.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **Third-largest**.

questions.question: In March 2026, India and Japan renewed their Bilateral Currency Swap Agreement for an additional three years. What is the value of this arrangement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**$75 Billion.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Agreement Renewal:** India and Japan renewed their **Bilateral Currency Swap Arrangement (BSA)** on March 4, 2026, for a further period of three years.
 
• **The Partners:** The renewal was formalized between the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and the **Bank of Japan (BoJ)**.
 
• **Total Value:** The facility provides for a swap amount of up to **$75 billion** (USD).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **How it Works__**

__
 
• **Mechanism:** Under this pact, India can swap its local currency (Rupees) for US Dollars or Japanese Yen, and vice versa, up to the $75 billion limit.
 
• **Purpose:** It serves as a **financial safety net** to address potential short-term liquidity challenges or balance-of-payments (BoP) stress.
 
• **Stability:** The arrangement helps in stabilizing the foreign exchange market and bolstering investor confidence during periods of global economic volatility.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Background & Strategic Importance__**

 
• **History:** This framework was first established in **2018** and was previously renewed in 2023. The 2026 renewal ensures continuity of the facility until 2029.
 
• **Indo-Pacific Ties:** The agreement is a pillar of the **India-Japan Special Strategic and Global Partnership**, reflecting deep mutual trust in financial cooperation.
 
• **Reserves Management:** While India maintains healthy foreign exchange reserves, this facility acts as a "second line of defense" without the need to draw down actual reserves.

questions.question: In March 2025, Operation Brahma was launched to assist earthquake hit __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Myanmar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Operation Brahma** was launched in **March 2025** by the Government of India to assist Myanmar after a devastating earthquake caused widespread destruction and loss of life.
 
• This operation was part of India’s commitment to providing humanitarian aid to its neighbors under its **"Neighborhood First" policy**.
 
• The assistance primarily included **rescue operations, medical aid, and relief supplies**, as Myanmar faced severe challenges due to the earthquake's aftermath.
 
• The operation was conducted with the support of Indian armed forces, medical teams, and disaster response units to ensure the swift delivery of aid.
 
• India has a history of supporting its neighbors during crises, reflecting its role as a responsible regional power and its strong bilateral ties with Myanmar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India-Myanmar Relations:**

 
 
• Myanmar shares a **1,643 km-long border** with India, touching four Indian states: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, and Mizoram.
 
• India and Myanmar have close historical, cultural, and economic ties. Myanmar is a key partner in India’s **Act East Policy**.
 
• The two countries have collaborated on infrastructure projects such as the **Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project** and the **India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway**.
 
 
 
• **Earthquake in Myanmar (March 2025):**
 
 
• The earthquake caused significant damage to infrastructure, homes, and public services, displacing thousands of people.
 
• Many areas were left without basic necessities such as food, water, and medical care, prompting international humanitarian responses.
 
 
 
• **India’s Disaster Assistance Framework:**
 
 
• India has a robust disaster response mechanism led by organizations such as the **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)** and the armed forces.
 
• India has previously launched similar missions like **Operation Maitri** to assist Nepal after the 2015 earthquake and **Operation Dost** to aid Turkey and Syria in 2023.
 
 
 
• **Neighborhood First Policy:**
 
 
• India’s Neighborhood First policy focuses on prioritizing relations with neighboring countries to ensure regional cooperation, stability, and development.
 
• Humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR) operations are an integral part of this policy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Operation Maitri (Nepal, 2015):**

 
 
• Conducted in response to the devastating earthquake in Nepal, providing rescue and relief operations.
 
• Included the deployment of the Indian Air Force and NDRF teams for search and rescue operations.
 
 
 
• **Operation Dost (Turkey and Syria, 2023):**
 
 
• India provided aid after the massive earthquake in Turkey and Syria, showcasing its commitment to global humanitarian efforts.
 
• Assistance included rescue teams, medical personnel, and essential supplies.
 
 
 
• **Disaster Response in India:**
 
 
• India has a comprehensive disaster response system led by the **Ministry of Home Affairs** and specialized agencies like the **NDRF**.
 
• India is recognized globally for its quick and efficient response to natural disasters in the region.

questions.question: During the 12th India-EU Human Rights Dialogue held in New Delhi in June 2026, which of the following did India reiterate as a distinct, universal, inalienable, and fundamental human right?

• **Shared Goal:** Both sides discussed their respective approaches and challenges in the advancement of human rights, covering civil, political, social, economic, and cultural rights.
• **Inclusivity:** The dialogue addressed the elimination of discrimination, the **rights of migrants**, freedom of religion, and the rights of **LGBTQI+** and children.

• The previous dialogue was held in **January 2025**, and the next dialogue is scheduled for **2027**.
• Both parties agreed to continue engagement through the **UN General Assembly** and the **UN Human Rights Council (UNHRC)**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding India's **'Operation Amistad'** is **INCORRECT**?

options.text: The operation was launched to provide humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR) to Venezuela after earthquakes of 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude.
India deployed a 41-member team from the Indian Army's 60 Para Field Hospital, which included nine medical officers.
As part of the emergency medical assistance, the Indian relief consignment included three BHISHM cube portable hospitals.
The relief supplies and rescue personnel were transported using two Indian Air Force (IAF) C-17 Globemaster aircraft.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**As part of the emergency medical assistance, the Indian relief consignment included three BHISHM cube portable hospitals.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
• **Statement 1 is correct:** The mission was initiated after **Venezuela** was hit by powerful earthquakes of **7.2 and 7.5 magnitude** on **June 24, 2026**, causing widespread destruction.
• **Statement 2 is correct:** A **41-member team** from the **60 Para Field Hospital** of the **Indian Army**, which includes **nine medical officers**, was deployed to support relief efforts.
• **Statement 3 is INCORRECT:** According to the official statement from the Ministry of External Affairs and EAM S. Jaishankar, India sent **two BHISHM cube** portable hospitals, not three.

questions.question: Which U.S.-led initiative did India officially join on 20 February 2026 to strengthen supply chain security in critical sectors?
questions.solution:

• **Pax Silica initiative:** India officially became a signatory to this **U.S.-led initiative** on **20 February 2026**. It is a core part of the ongoing cooperation to strengthen **supply chain security** in critical sectors.
 
• **Framework on Critical Minerals:** The main framework discussed in the news was signed by External Affairs Minister **Dr. S. Jaishankar** and U.S. Secretary of State **Marco Rubio** to deepen cooperation in **mining, processing, and recycling**.
 
• **Forum on Resource Geostrategic Engagement (FORGE):** This is another initiative under which India and the U.S. are partnering, but it was not the specific initiative signed on **20 February 2026**.

• The primary goal of these agreements is to establish **resilient and diversified supply chains** for **rare earths** and **critical minerals**, which are essential for **emerging technologies** and **advanced manufacturing**.
